annotations.text:
Where the leaderboards and achievements are reached from.

Both open the platform's own screen - the Play Games overlay on Android, Game Center on iOS - on top of the game. There is no leaderboard or achievement screen inside Flexi Run itself.

All three entry points appear only while signed in. Signed out, the pill is the SIGN IN slab, there is no trophy, and the best-score line is plain text.

The gameplay screen.

A wall is on screen for 7.5 seconds, but for most of that it is small and far away, and its hole is a dark opening on red-brown brick. A child has to read circle-vs-square-vs-star from a silhouette alone - and the pad buttons are white because, correctly, a coloured button would teach a cue the wall could not answer.

The change is to let the wall answer it. Rim the hole in the shape's own colour. The opening stays genuinely open - meadow shows through it exactly as now - so the rule that the hole is a real transparent opening still holds. Only the edge is painted.

Every screen in the game, at 800x360 - the real logical size of your phone.

These are drawn from the code as it stands after today's changes, not from imagination: the slab gradients, the white rim, the parchment level pills and the faces are the ones now on your phone. Colours and sizes come out of constants.dart.

Already true on your phone: 1 (Home), and 2 (Paused) as of today.

Partly true: 3. The panel buttons route through the same ChunkyButton, so the end-of-run slabs picked up the rim, gradient, gloss and lit top with the pause panel.

Not yet built: 4, 5.

In play has a page of its own - see the Gameplay screen tab.

It is the one screen the menu's slab language deliberately does not reach: the pad tiles lie over live gameplay, and a solid tile takes a bite out of the road the player is reading.

Two things on 5 and 6 that are proposals, not recreations.

HOW TO PLAY gains a picture strip under the four steps: shape, arrow, wall, tick. The words are one sentence each and a six year old may not read any of them; the strip says the same thing without words.

SETTINGS gains a Tap anywhere switch. CLAUDE.md lists it as a real setting, on by default - it has never had a control, and the sheet has the room.

Details worth keeping whichever way you go.

The end-of-run panel never says "game over". The run ended and the next one starts from the button below it; six year olds put the phone down when told they lost.

The gold slab says the word "ad". A child pressing it is agreeing to watch one, and the button should be what tells them.

Sound sits on the pause panel as well as in Settings, because mid-run in a quiet room is where a parent actually reaches for it.

Four changes, in order of how much they matter.

1. The hole gets a rim in its shape's colour. Look at the small far wall: today that is a dark patch, and the shape is a guess until it is close. This is the one that buys reaction time.

2. The pad buttons take those same three colours. Only possible because of 1 - otherwise it teaches a cue the wall cannot answer.

3. The tiles get denser and gain the white rim the menu slabs now carry. At 0.56 alpha over bright beige path their edge vanishes exactly where a child aims.

4. The score grows and the coin count joins it. The score is what the run is for and it is currently smaller than a heart.
